this-war-of-mine game sourced

This War of Mine

A survival sim about civilians in a besieged city who maintain a shelter by day, scavenge by night, and face moral choices that change their mood until a randomized ceasefire.

201411 bit studiosSurvival simcluster c1412 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

spend the day in the shelter crafting, cooking, trading, and treating -> assign night roles -> one survivor scavenges a location -> encounters force moral choices -> hunger, wounds, illness, and mood shift -> survive until the ceasefire

design notes

The game turns war into a resource-and-conscience problem: survival needs push the player toward theft or violence, and those acts lower survivors' mood, so material and moral states are coupled. A day-night split separates base management (snipers keep survivors inside by day) from risky scavenging by one chosen survivor, and the length of the war is randomized so the player cannot plan to a known end. The radio reports weather, prices, and war news that let the player anticipate shortages. It draws on the 1992-96 Siege of Sarajevo.

12 stored edges
uses

Day-night cycle

Snipers confine survivors to the shelter by day for crafting, cooking, and care; at night survivors are assigned to sleep, guard, or scavenge.

core
uses

Dilemma cards

Scavenging encounters and visitors at the door pose choices, such as robbing vulnerable NPCs or giving away supplies, that trade material gain against mood and each survivor's ending.

core
uses

Mood and breakdowns

Mood falls with hunger, illness, loss of companions, and morally weighted acts such as stealing or killing; depressed or broken survivors refuse tasks and may leave the shelter or take their own lives.

core
uses

Needs decay

Each survivor tracks hunger, fatigue, health, and mood, and the player must keep them up until the ceasefire.

core
uses

Forecasting

Radio broadcasts give weather warnings, economic updates, and war news.
